newsitem.title: USA: Productivity fell in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Productivity fell in third quarter.

text.p: American business productivity fell in the third quarter, showing more weakness than previously reported, the government said Thursday.
The Labour Department said productivity outside of the agricultural sector dropped 0.3 percent in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with preliminary estimates that showed it edging up 0.2 percent.
The decline exceeded the 0.1 percent drop forecast by Wall Street economists.
The drop was the first since a 1.2 percent decline during the fourth quarter of 1995, the department said. In the second quarter of 1996, productivity jumped 0.6 percent.
The department said productivity suffered as hours worked rose 2.1 percent but output grew by only 1.8 percent.

Unit labour costs, which make up two-thirds of businesses' production costs, rose at an unrevised 3.7 percent rate in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 3.3 percent in the previous quarter.

Non-farm productivity data provide a reading on the efficiency of business by measuring the amount of goods and services produced per hour by all workers. Strong growth in productivity allows wages to rise proportionately without a pickup in inflation.
